To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size distribution of dynamic content can be approximated by a Pareto distribution, the distribution of object lifetimes is well approximated by a Weibull distribution, and the reusability of content across objects and documents is highly correlated with object size.
the object characteristics of Web content vary significantly across sites and that the object characteristics are not correlated with the freshness characteristics.

(1) the characteristics of dynamic Web objects can be effectively modeled using a small number of parameters and (2) these models can be used to generate realistic synthetic content that can serve as a test bed for evaluating the effectiveness of proposed solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of models for dynamic content and a tool to help researchers and practitioners evaluate and compare techniques for improving the efficiency of Web servers and caches in serving dynamic content.

developing models that capture the structure and behavior of dynamic content, and using these models as a foundation for developing synthetic content generators that can be used to evaluate the performance of new caching techniques and to drive the development of new techniques.
understanding the characteristics of Web content and developing techniques for modeling, measuring, and generating dynamic content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed models provide a good characterization of the dynamic content of the sites considered in the paper and the proposed generator can generate synthetic dynamic content that is similar to the original.

the proposed models and the dynamic content emulator are effective tools to model and emulate dynamic Web content and can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of different techniques for dynamic content caching and distribution.
this paper presents the first comprehensive study of dynamic content and the first dynamic content generator that is able to produce realistic content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a set of tools that can be used for evaluating and comparing different caching and distribution solutions for dynamic content.

we have proposed models for dynamic Web content that are based on real-world traces and can be used to generate dynamic Web content for testing and evaluating caching and content distribution systems.

we provide a comprehensive set of models to describe the characteristics of dynamic Web documents and we provide a content emulator that generates synthetic dynamic Web documents that follow the characteristics of real dynamic Web documents.
